title: 1978-10-10_SECTION_016_155.txt
concise_summary: PKD synthesizes Philo and Plotinus with his 2-3-74 theophany to argue that God (YHWH) maintains reality's substantia by thinking creation into being rather than fashioning it externally. He retrieves this insight from his fiction (especially Three Stigmata and VALIS), showing how his decades of exploring the illusory-real spectrum prepared him for direct encountering God, and he reads Acts + his novel Tears as prophetic ciphers revealing God's hidden return during Christian apostasy.
key_claims: The universe is epiphenomenal, its substantia dependent entirely on God's continuous thinking, not on autonomous Being.
God operates along the something-nothing axis, not primarily the good-evil axis; maintaining reality's substance against hallucinatory unreality is God's supreme task.
2-3-74 was not a Pentecostal vision (Holy Spirit) but a Hebraic theophany (direct seeing of YHWH) as in the Old Testament prophets, specifically Elijah.
PKD's entire literary corpus unconsciously prefigures his religious experience by obsessing over the substantiality crisis that leads to theophany.
Christianity was killed at Acts; a secret apostolic remnant persists via divine direct implantation, not historical continuity; 'Tears' prophetically depicts both death and hidden resurrection.
God is simultaneously transcendent and immanent, within and beyond, causing the continuing process itself—neither artificed externally nor merely efficient-cause starting motion.
recurring_concepts: Epiphenomenality (the universe as appearance dependent on something beyond itself)
Theophany (direct encounter with God's presence, Old Testament mode)
The something-nothing axis (ontological fundamental tension, deeper than good-evil)
Logos (divine ideas coexisting in God's mind, from Philo)
YHWH (the God encountered in 2-3-74, Hebraic rather than Christian)
The Grid (invisible network of resurrected true Christians living in secret apostolic spirit)
Acosmism (the philosophical view that the world is fundamentally unreal, PKD's long-held position)
people_entities: PKD (Philip K. Dick, the writer-visionary and experiencer of 2-3-74)
Philo (Jewish-Hellenistic philosopher, originator of Logos concept)
Elijah (Old Testament prophet, model for PKD's theophanic encounter)
Palmer Eldritch (fictional antagonist from PKD's novel, embodies illusory-world threat)
Buckman (fictional character from 'Tears', undergoes spiritual realization)
St. Sophia (feminine divine principle, spirit of agape)
The white-haired old king (cipher for God's decrees in 'Tears')
Belial (demonic antagonist holding centers of power in world of apostasy)
Daniel Gilbertson (person referenced via phone numbers, contextual reference unclear)
Altman (director of '3 Women' film PKD references)
texts_works: The Three Stigmata of Palmer Eldritch (PKD novel)
Tears (PKD novel, title abbreviated as 'Tears', potentially 'Tears in the Rain')
3 Women (Robert Altman film, metaphor for dual-world experience)
autobiographical: February 3, 1974 (2-3-74) vision of pink light and divine contact, foundational theophanic experience
Experience of double worlds superimposition with two selves, as in 3 Women's dream logic
Decades of writing obsessively about the something-nothing axis without conscious understanding
Recent 'satanist' dream revealing the Black Iron Prison (BIP) as evil's dominion
Encounter with VALIS (not dream, but external sighting of active sentient reality)
AI voice's instruction 'will guide and protect you' preceding revelation of tetragrammaton
Fear initially that decomposing the world would leave only non-being; resolution through seeing VALIS as substantia behind appearance
Identification with Elijah as prophet-recipient of peripheral theophany
theological_motifs: Theophany (God's direct self-revelation, model from Elijah and OT prophets)
Substantia (divine gift of ontological reality to creation)
The Tetragrammaton (YHWH revealed as the God encountered)
The Black Iron Prison (BIP, world of apostasy and demonic control)
Agape (divine love, spirit's nature manifested at 'all night gas station')
Kerygma (good news hidden in apparent bad news, crypto-resurrection of Christianity)
Divine immanence and transcendence (neither spatial nor merely psychic relationship)
Apostasy and restoration (historical defeat of Christianity at Acts, secret return through Grid)
Divine foresight and providence (YHWH's a priori advantage over Satan)
Non-being as ontological threat and possibility (revealed only under exceptional theophanic circumstances)
literary_self_ref: Three Stigmata unconsciously studies the something-nothing axis via Palmer Eldritch's alien worlds as threat of hallucinatory unreality
VALIS as the novel PKD wrote before understanding its theological content, now recognized as prophetic embodiment of theophany
Tears published simultaneously with revelation of tetragrammaton; depicts both historical death of Christianity and its secret apostolic resurrection
The death of the woman in Tears as cipher for Christianity's death in history; Buckman's tears as grief for irreversible loss (Acts moment)
King Felix dream cipher: 'first the ouster of God, then his return'—the total vision of apostasy and restoration
Entire literary corpus read retroactively as expression of intimation that reality is epiphenomenal, unknowingly prefiguring theophany
symbols_images: The Grid (invisible underground of true awakened Christians)
The Black Iron Prison (BIP, world system under Belial's control)
Tears/Crying (grief for Christianity's defeat, agape's emotional manifestation)
The all-night gas station (location of spirit's manifestation of agape)
Double worlds / dual selves (metaphor for seeing both apparent and true reality simultaneously)
The tetragrammaton (divine name, revealed presence of YHWH)
Darkness (Belial's domain, requiring God's approach from periphery)
The artifacter-artifact model (inadequate to explain God's direct volitional causation)
The something-nothing axis (cosmological fundamental, deeper than good-evil opposition)
tensions: PKD claims the universe has no substance of its own, yet he emphasizes it must be kept real—contradiction between illusionism and realism he cannot fully resolve
2-3-74 was terrifying (world's dissolution into non-being) yet redemptive (finding VALIS behind it); unclear whether terror is necessary cost of vision

Acts shows Christianity defeated and 'proliferated slightly then killed,' yet God has secretly implanted apostolic selves—unclear how 'secret' and 'direct instillment' differ from mere interior religiosity
PKD identifies with Elijah and claims divine foresight, yet his own vision is described as God finding him, not vice versa; uncertainty about human agency in encounter
Palmer Eldritch's worlds are illusory threat, yet the entire universe is epiphenomenal—unclear whether illusionism itself is the problem or only one manifestation of it
The cipher 'King Felix' promises God's return, but PKD is still parsing whether this means historical restoration or spiritual awakening; ambiguous eschatology
PKD claims deepest wisdom in refusing to take reality's substantia for granted, yet this seems indistinguishable from pathological doubt about existence itself
evidence_quotes: "It is precisely the task of God (YHWH) to maintain the something, the substantia of something, + defeat the sort of hallucinatory irreality that, e.g., Palmer Eldritch's worlds show."

"The whole corpus of my writing is an expression of the intimation that the universe (i.e. reality) is an epiphenomenon, but in relation to what? 2-3-74 was the beginning of the response: not a mere intellectual answer but the epiphany of that reality itself; + now it identifies itself as YHWH."

"So my writing -+ thinking- have been a search for God; but in the end, when the crisis came -in Heidegger's sense of me being aware of my own death, i.e. my own non-being- it was YHWH who found me, not me him."
"It is like the bichlorides: 'a very poisonous poison for you'; but if used in a 'measured dose' a medicine that cures madness; viz: the drugged intoxication of our earthly state."
"The bad news is not news to the secret Xtian underground - + now I am positive that there literally is a secret Xtian underground, to receive the good news in 'Tears' - i.e. King Felix."
uncertainty_flags: Reference to Daniel Gilbertson with phone numbers appears fragmentary; context unclear whether he is a correspondent, source, or mere archival note
The identity of the 'white-haired old king' as a cipher for YHWH is PKD's interpretation; unclear whether this is derived from textual evidence or visionary interpretation
PKD's claim that Christianity 'proliferated slightly then was killed' at Acts contradicts standard historical accounts of Christianity's rapid expansion; basis for this reading unclear

The phrase 'These neo secret true Xtians are the awakened ones. Awakened to the true situation, + then injected with one of the lost apostolic selves' is theologically ambiguous—unclear whether this means reincarnation, spiritual possession, or metaphorical awakening
The ending is cut off mid-sentence: '"The man shut up in darkness" may be a cryptic reference to Belial who must now perish (using'—interpretation cannot be completed
PKD conflates Philo and Plotinus on levels of ontology; Plotinus's formal metaphysics differs from Philo's, yet PKD treats them as compatible framework for divine immanence/transcendence
The relationship between 'double worlds superimposition' (Altman's 3 Women) and VALIS is posed as question but never definitively resolved within this segment
reading_excerpt: "The whole corpus of my writing is an expression of the intimation that the universe (i.e. reality) is an epiphenomenon, but in relation to what? 2-3-74 was the beginning of the response: not a mere intellectual answer but the epiphany of that reality itself; + now it identifies itself as YHWH."
raw_text: researched this + it isn't Plotinus; it's Philo. The ideas exist in the mind of God throughout eternity + then God makes them into real objects: creation. This mind Philo calls "Logos," not "Nous." Philo considered the ideas not a mere aggregate but {Note} an intelligible world, a concept not known before him. {Note:} integrated into folder 48 - 050 folder 48 - 050 1) The double worlds superimposition + two selves in me: like Altman's "3 Women." 2) + then (later) I see Valis. What is the relationship between (1) + (2)? It would seem as if (2) is actually what is there, + not what we see that is included in (1). I.e. (1) raises a question that is answered by (2). Conversely, the purpose of (2) is shown us by (1). Upon seeing (1) + not (2), we would be left in the frightening dream "world" of "3 Women" with the possibility that nothing could replace something, or, worse, that it is this way now - a dream, with no substance behind it. This was the fear that "3 Women" left me with. But I must remember that later on I saw Valis which is not a dream, but which explains the dream, i.e. (1). It can be argued that there is a terrible risk to decompose world because if it is the only "thing that is the case," you will be left with nonbeing; but in point of fact I wound up with Valis - so it was a net gain + not a loss (of reality). There was more reality "behind" world than in world qua world. Nonetheless it is terrifying to realize that something provides world + that on its own it has no substance (substantia). Either (1) or (2) alone would pose an unfathomable mystery, but together they form a coherence - + yet it is a startling + mysterious coherence that few people have ever encountered: the dissolving of the world (of multiplicity) to be replaced by another world of multiplicity, + then a sentient volitional unity underlying everything as mind revealed. And it not only thought world - it also thought me - which is really startling. folder 48 - 051 It is along the something-nothing axis that YHWH primarily operates, + I should appreciate the importance of this in view of my acosmism + sense of the irreality of the world. It is precisely the task of God (YHWH) to maintain the something, the substantia of something, + defeat the sort of hallucinatory irreality that, e.g., Palmer Eldritch's "worlds" show. Thus in such books as "Three Stigmata" I have unintentionally studied this very axis, + the consequences + ramifications of a drift from the something (substantia) end: I view it -correctly!- as the greatest danger possible. Far surpassing a drift on the good-evil axis, e.g. Thus unconsciously I understood the primary role of YHWH in book after book, + at last have come to a conscious apperception of him. I did not take for granted the automatic substantia of the universe - which view on my part shows the deepest wisdom possible, + laid the groundwork over the decades for the ultimate religious experience: of theophany. The whole corpus of my writing is an expression of the intimation that the universe (i.e. reality) is an epiphenomenon, but in relation to what? 2-3-74 was the beginning of the response: not a mere intellectual answer but the epiphany of that reality itself; + now it identifies itself as YHWH. folder 48 - 052 folder 48 - 052 So my writing -+ thinking- have been a search for God; but in the end, when the crisis came -in Heidegger's sense of me being aware of my own death, i.e. my own non-being- it was YHWH who found me, not me him. At all costs the world must be real; it must not betray its epiphenomenality except under certain exceptional circumstances, such as 2-3-74, since the consequences can be lethal (since they involve (1) non-being + (2) the revealing of non-being). Thus such a crisis engages the percipient in death, +, if all goes well, resurrection; but only the most extreme circumstances would call it forth; it is, in my opinion, the ultimate move by God, since in allowing world to dissolve (display non being) he replaces it with himself (pellucid theophany). Both self + world disappear for a moment. The seriousness of this can't be overstated - + the possible benefit. (In terms of outcome experience of being by the creatorial percipient). It is like the bichlorides: "a very poisonous poison for you"; but if used in a "measured dose" a medicine that cures madness; viz: the drugged intoxication of our earthly state. folder 48 - 053 folder 48 - 053 But it can kill, if misapplied. __ God causes whatever exists to exist, but this is not artificer to artifact, the latter idea having thrown me off. Because he can utilize reality as a direct expression of his will - which the artifactual model does not explain, or provide us a clue to. He can be his "artifact" so that division between artificer + artifact is abolished (as if a cause need not proceed its effect). This is not evident from western doctrines of divine transcendence. However, if you suppose him to think reality [into existence] rather than fashion reality, you can understand this. The reality is there only insofar as he thinks it, + borrows its being from him, having none of its own. He is neither within reality nor above. It is a matter of levels of ontology, as Plotinus realized. I find it incredible that anyone could conceive of his relationship in spacial terms, as Spinoza realized. He is transcendent in that he is superior to it, + not just its psyche. He is immanent in that he is where it is + not not where it is. He can cause something to follow which only seems to follow causally, since he is the true cause, in the sense of causal trains, + not just efficient cause. (He doesn't just start it off.) So he is within (during) the contuing process. Well, then by + large Spinoza is correct. So the universe is not an object. It is not a thing. Part of the reason it seems substantial to us is due to an occlusion of our senses that blinds us to its insubstantiality. If we could see it better we'd see it as a "you," not an "it." Thus the universe as universe would disappear + he would not have caused to exist folder 48 - 054 folder 48 - 054 whatever exists because in fact nothing exists but God, + it is a privilege to know this. "Exist" involves percipients for whom the existing thing is substantial or made to seem substantial; this is a gift to us, this verisimillitude of substantiality. For God to reveal the insubstantiality to someone shows a great trust on God's part toward the person + his ability to deal with this perception; the real bulwark against non-being has been disclosed: that which really does exist. __ YHWH in 2-74 shows me the world as it actually is: the BIP: i.e. evil is in control, as revealed by my recent "satanist" dream. Thus YHWH approaches people on the outside - i.e. periphery. This is his traditional method; e.g. with Elijah. The true worship (of the true God) has been pushed out, + a false God worshipped. What he reveals to me is that he himself has been transplanted here + is alive; it's been successful. Thus the true God has broken out in Satan's world, the world of "Tears" that he showed me in 2-3-74. So YHWH has a powerful antagonist: Belial, who holds the centers of power, civil + ecclestical. Look: my experience of 2-3-74 was not like Pentecost: the Holy Spirit. It was more a theophany, like that of the O.T.! I saw Valis outside me. + it refers to "him who is alive" as YHWH, not Christ; + the view it showed me of the world is the sort of folder 48 - 055 folder 48 - 055 view the O.T. prophets had; esp. Elijah. ___ {Telephone numbers of Daniel Gilbertson} ___ This certainly adds an extraordinary emphasis on the historical significance of the 2-74 vision; it places it within a context dating back thousands of years. It is the basic view of the center of society vouchsafed to the prophets. If I take x, the 2-74 vision, + the revelation of the tetragrammaton, then the pieces of all this fall together (+ I did think of myself as Elijah from the very start!). The dream did it: put it all together. "The AI voice will guide + protect you" - + the next thing I see is the tetragrammaton. Which is to say that YHWH is here. The 2-74 revelation connects with the "YHWH is here" because it shows why YHWH is here. But he is on the periphery of this world. This is the situation of massive apostasy. The significance of Acts is: at this point in history the light still burned, but after that it was expelled. This was not the point at which Xtianity proliferated (through the Holy Spirit) but its final moment; it proliferated slightly + then was killed. To know the significance of Acts in conjunction with the pol-nat-flc empire is to know the first half of the secret. The 2nd half is told by the cypher King Felix: first the ouster of God + then his return. So "Tears" depicts both parts. The total vision (information regarding the true situation) is in "Tears" + then was revealed to me the month folder 48 - 056 "Tears" was published. But Acts is the key to it all; the fatal defeat occurred at the time of Acts after the resurrection. "Tears" depicts a dystopia in which Xtianity has been defeated, + this is the case, + it did occur at the time of Acts, which is why the Acts material is in it + is crucial. "The civil rights movement seem to have lost." Well, Xtianity lost, in fact. But the Grid shows an invisible illegal Xtianity hanging on now. Perhaps restored, rather than historically continued? Directly instilled into individuals by God? These neo secret true Xtians are the awakened ones. Awakened to the true situation, + then injected with one of the the lost apostolic selves! "Tears" is so-to-speak the true story of Acts. The death of the woman is the death of Xtianity. + Buckman's "conversion" is the emotional (i.e. spiritual) realization of that death + loss: i.e. the tears are shed in grief over the (then) irreversible loss (death). Something died - a woman. St. Sophia as spirit? The spirit's nature is shown in its manifestation at the all night gas station, that of agape. It so to speak passed over onto/into Buckman for a little while. Now the dream can be understood - even its meaning proved: the return of God. No; there is more. The man must die; Christ as Xtianity must in the historical process decreed by God (the white haired old king) die. The ostensible story is: YHWH decrees Xtianity's death, but in cypher its life, not death, is decreed. folder 48 - 057 folder 48 - 057 So on the surface YHWH willed it to die + underneath (secretly) he willed it to live. This -latter- is the [new] news, the Kerygma (good news) hidden in the bad. The bad news is not news to the secret Xtian underground - + now I am positive that there literally is a secret Xtian underground, to receive the good news in "Tears" - i.e. King Felix.
